False positive: the target callback guards and chooses the printed reference Effect Monster. The operation does not make a second selection; Duel.GetMatchingGroup intentionally enumerates the distinct printed group of all other face-up Effect Monsters sharing a characteristic with that chosen monster, so its dgfilter predicate must differ from the activation guard.
rmfilter validates that each banishable card has the corresponding named summon available; the later spfilter selection uses the code determined by the card actually banished.

Activation checks for at least one negatable monster and draw legality. Resolution enumerates all face-up monsters, applies the negate predicate individually, then counts the opponent's current face-up monsters.
The activation search is optional, so the card may be activated with no target. Resolution correctly applies Necrovalley legality before offering and selecting the search.
tgfilter only accepts a first Deck monster when another same-name copy is available. The operation then uses samefilter for the required second copy.

The cost returns this monster to hand and frees its Main Monster Zone. recruittg uses precruitfilter with the pre-cost released monster and a prospective self-Summon check; recruitop uses spfilter on the post-cost state. Both filters enforce the same archetype, monster, face-up Extra Deck and Summonability constraints; the zone predicates intentionally differ across payment.

eqtg targets a GY equip candidate through eqfilter. eqfilter itself requires an existing canEquipTo recipient. eqop refilters targeted cards through eqfilter before choosing that recipient, and rechecks Spell/Trap zone capacity per card. The recipient search is guarded transitively through the target filter.

This optional activation follow-up is chosen in acttg only if activationvictim exists; that predicate requires a destructible card and both retrieval destinations (including a victim that will reach GY). actop checks its activation label and card relation, selects a destructible victim, then separately rechecks both retrieval pools after destruction. The broad resolution selection is intentional, not an unguarded mandatory activation.

The activation requires deslegal, which combines the same desfilter with prospective zone availability after destruction. Resolution selects with desfilter, destroys it, then independently rechecks the two-monster Summon legality and two free zones before Summoning. Different predicates account for the prospective and actual post-destruction states.

Beacon may move a monster even when its new co-linked counter-recipient group is empty. Movement legality is checked at activation; the optional resulting recipients are computed after movement. Native engine movement and counter cases verify both empty and populated groups.

Surge checks a free pointed zone and supporting Ohmenchanic at activation, then recomputes the surviving pointed zones at resolution. It correctly does nothing if the source or required graph is lost. Thirteen delayed-trigger engine cases verify interruptions and zone changes.

Activation uses s.options to validate selectable mode. The own-monster search occurs only in a banish-selected mode and both own and opposing removable monster groups are explicitly rechecked immediately before selection.

The target uses spacefilter, which includes desfilter and proves a zone exists or can be opened by the victim. Resolution selects the MZONE subset when needed, otherwise desfilter, then checks actual destruction and free zone before summoning.

The target uses spacefilter including destroyfilter and prospective zone opening. Resolution narrows to an MZONE victim when full, checks actual destruction, related source and available zone before revival; the optional opponent overlay is independently guarded.
